title: Mebendazole induces ZBP-1 mediated PANoptosis of acute myeloid leukemia cells by targeting TUBA1A and exerts antileukemia effect.
authors: Yang, Wei; Xu, Ying; Liu, Shuai; Gao, Lin; Li, Shi; Xie, Xina; Zhang, Qiaoxia; Habib, Obaid; Chen, Ronglin; Sun, Xiongfei; Li, Zesong
one_liner_zh: 该文研究甲苯咪唑通过靶向TUBA1A诱导AML细胞PANoptosis的抗白血病作用，属于药物机制与肿瘤治疗研究，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite notable advancements in AML therapy in recent years, a substantial proportion of patients remain refractory or at high risk of recurrence with limited efficacy. Therefore, it's urgent to develop novel drugs for treating AML. METHODS: The small molecule drug library was utilized to screen for drugs that elicit the inflammatory death of AML cells. Cell viability, cell morphological analysis, western blotting, and RNA-seq were used to determine the pathway of Mebendazole (MBD)-induced AML cell death. Cell cycle analysis, protein expression profiling, molecular docking, western blotting and lentivirus overexpression were used to analyze the target protein of MBD in AML cells. The anti-AML activity of MBD in vivo was evaluated using tumor xenograft models constructed by AML cell lines and patient-derived primary AML cells. RESULTS: In this study, we have identified Mebendazole (MBD), a conventional anthelmintic drug known for its low toxicity and cost, as a potent agent that exerts significant anti-AML effects in vitro. Furthermore, we have observed its inhibitory effects on the invasion of AML cell lines and primary AML cells in xenograft mouse models, while noting its negligible toxic side effects in normal mice in vivo. Mechanically, MBD inhibits the cell cycle in G2/M phase by inhibiting tubulin alpha1A (TUBA1A) and promotes ZBP-1 mediated PANoptosis in AML cells. Our results confirm that MBD exerts anti-AML activity in preclinical models. CONCLUSION: These results highlight the remarkable clinical translational potential of MBD, providing new potential medicine for AML patients. In addition, TUBA1A can be used potential novel therapeutic target in tumors with abnormal TUBA1A expression.
abstract_zh: 背景：尽管近年来急性髓系白血病（AML）治疗取得了显著进展，但仍有相当比例的患者对治疗无效或处于高复发风险中，疗效有限。因此，开发治疗AML的新型药物迫在眉睫。方法：利用小分子药物库筛选能诱导AML细胞发生炎症性死亡的药物。通过细胞活力、细胞形态学分析、蛋白质印迹法和RNA-seq确定甲苯咪唑（MBD）诱导AML细胞死亡的途径。采用细胞周期分析、蛋白表达谱分析、分子对接、蛋白质印迹法和慢病毒过表达技术分析MBD在AML细胞中的靶蛋白。利用AML细胞系和患者来源的原代AML细胞构建的肿瘤异种移植模型评估MBD在体内的抗AML活性。结果：在本研究中，我们鉴定出甲苯咪唑（MBD）——一种以低毒性和低成本著称的传统抗寄生虫药物——作为在体外具有显著抗AML效应的强效药物。此外，我们观察到其在异种移植小鼠模型中对AML细胞系和原代AML细胞侵袭的抑制作用，同时注意到其在正常小鼠体内具有可忽略的毒性副作用。机制上，MBD通过抑制微管蛋白α1A（TUBA1A）来阻断细胞周期于G2/M期，并促进AML细胞中ZBP-1介导的PANoptosis。我们的结果证实MBD在临床前模型中具有抗AML活性。结论：这些结果凸显了MBD显著的临床转化潜力，为AML患者提供了新的潜在药物。此外，TUBA1A可作为TUBA1A表达异常的肿瘤中潜在的新型治疗靶点。
